title: I've got to control the lows
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you are down, who makes your decisions: your feelings, or you?

groups.heading: I've got to control the lows

lines.text: What kind of decisions are you going to make in your lows, Jose asked? A student answered: ones out of those feelings, which would probably be bad decisions.
That's right, he said. I was a roller coaster in my twenties. I learned over the years: when I'm in the trough, when things are looking bad, I've got to control the lows and stay positive.
I would just do my mantras and my positive thinking, he said. It is discipline, not letting myself go to those lows.

Do I have reasons to go into the lows? I have debts, I have this crisis. I don't let my brain go there, because that is not going to help me. What helps is: this is how I'm going to make this money, this is what I'm going to focus on.
Good decisions come from good logical thinking, with your conviction, he said.

Jose asked: can I take a risk, suffer a crisis, and come out of it? What is my perspective? Am I going to make decisions from a position of strength, or from a position where I'm weakened and my perspective of myself is down and low?
A student who works with hotel guests said: it's not a crisis unless you make it a crisis. Figure out what they need and get to the solution. Jose said you learn how to calm people down.

groups.heading: Who stays on the boat with us?

lines.text: The takeaways, Jose said. Who are we in moments of crisis? How do we handle the highs and the lows? And what do we do to make decisions from a position of strength, from clarity, no matter what is happening in our external environment?
He asks people: what if we were in a lifeboat without food or water, all together? Who would be the leader? Who would panic? Who would sneak the food and not share it? How would we ration the water?

Look around and analyze who is with you in those moments, he said. Who is with you in the lows? Who is with you in the company when it goes down? Who has those strong convictions to go all the way with you? Who stays on the boat with us?
Who stays on the boat with you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a low you are in, or were in recently, in one line.
Write the story your feelings tell you about it.
Write what you will focus on instead: how you will make it work.
Write a mantra or a sentence you will say to yourself.
Write the names of the people who stay on the boat with you.

check.q: What did a student say decisions made from your feelings in the lows would be?
What did Jose say helps in the lows?
choices: Focusing on how you will make it work

check.q: Which question did Jose say he asks people about a lifeboat?
choices: Who would be the leader and who would panic?

recap: Control the lows. Decide from a position of strength.
